Announcing the NeurIPS 2026 Affinity Events

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference affinity-workshops, neurips2026

By Celia Cintas, Harshita Sahni, Sarthak Arora, Yachna Sharma

We are excited to announce this year’s affinity events co-located with NeurIPS in Sydney (Australia), Paris (France), and Atlanta (United States).

What are affinity groups?

At NeurIPS, affinity groups play a crucial role in promoting and supporting the ideas and voices of various communities that are defined by some axis of joint identity and raise awareness of issues that affect their members. In addition, they provide members of these affinity groups with increased opportunities to showcase their work, engage in discussions, and build connections during NeurIPS events, promoting diversity and inclusion at NeurIPS.

The main goals of affinity events are to increase visibility of the work done by the members of the affinity group, enable them to interact and discuss topics that are unique to each affinity group, and encourage affinity group members to showcase their work and step into the NeurIPS community.  In contrast to regular workshops, affinity group workshops adopt a more open and flexible approach around topic areas, focusing on forming research communities within the affinity groups and bringing attention to the unique challenges faced by their members.

Additionally, affinity group socials serve as safe and welcoming spaces, allowing members to interact, socialize, and network in an inclusive environment. By fostering such social gatherings, NeurIPS supports the creation of a supportive community that values diversity and ensures that all voices are heard and valued.

What kind of events do affinity groups offer at conferences?

Affinity groups organize events with the main aim of encouraging people to showcase their work and step into the NeurIPS community. The affinity events at NeurIPS this year will take place throughout the main conference week and across three different venues: Paris, Sydney, and Atlanta. See below for the details on when each affinity event will take place. NeurIPS will offer streaming support for all the in-person components of the affinity groups. 

What can NeurIPS attendees do to support affinity groups?

Participate! Actively attending and participating in panels and sessions for discussions about issues that are relevant to the affinity groups goes a long way in helping promote their cause. We request all members of our community to participate actively!

Affinity groups at NeurIPS 2026

We are delighted to announce the following affinity groups at NeurIPS 2026 at the main venue in Sydney as well as Satellite events in Paris and Atlanta. Find out more below about their mission and the event they are organizing! 

Africa in AI

The Africa in AI Affinity Workshop will be held for the first time as part of NeurIPS. The workshop will establish a dedicated forum for AI researchers, practitioners, industry partners, and policymakers working at the intersection of AI and sustainable development in Africa. By bringing together diverse disciplines and stakeholders across Africa’s socio-political and innovation ecosystems, the Affinity Group and its workshop will foster dialogue on the opportunities and challenges associated with AI adoption in the region, including shared constraints related to infrastructure, skilled personnel, funding, governance, and institutional capacity. 

This inaugural workshop emphasizes cross-disciplinary collaborations to address interconnected development priorities, such as health and climate resilience or sustainable cities and productive employment, with the goal of advancing scalable and resource-efficient AI solutions in the region. Through the Africa in AI Affinity Group, we are building a pan-African community that will showcase African perspectives, highlight region-specific challenges, and provide opportunities to elevate innovations on trustworthy AI that supports sustainable development outcomes. Ultimately, the Affinity Group aims to strengthen the African AI ecosystem and accelerate the responsible adoption of AI technologies that contribute to peace, prosperity, and inclusive development across the continent.

Africa in AI will be present only at the Atlanta venue on December 9th. 

For more details on the Africa in AI Affinity Group and event, visit our website: https://africainai.mailab.io/

GlobalSouthAI 

The GlobalSouthAI affinity event brings together AI/ML researchers working under resource constraints across the Global South. These communities face structural limitations in compute, data access, infrastructure, and research mobility, yet contribute significantly to efficient and robust ML systems. Our goal is to establish a sustained NeurIPS-affiliated community focused on efficient, inclusive, and context-aware ML systems, and to strengthen collaboration between Global South and Global North researchers. We are committed to creating a safe, inclusive environment for networking, mentorship, and technical exchange among researchers who are systematically underrepresented at NeurIPS. The community builds on two highly successful predecessor events, GlobalSouthAI @ AAAI 2026 (100+ submissions) and GlobalSouthML @ ICML 2026 (150+ submissions), demonstrating strong demand and community engagement. The one-day program features invited talks from leading researchers across academia and industry, lightning talks, a Three-Minute Thesis (3MT) competition, and a poster session showcasing cutting-edge research. The event focuses on technical challenges in resource-constrained ML systems, including efficient training, deployment under limited compute, multilingual and low-resource modeling, and data governance in constrained environments.  All invited speakers and organizers will attend in person. GlobalSouthAI will be present across Paris and Sydney venues: 

Sydney – December 7th

Paris –  December 9th 

For more details, please visit our website: https://sites.google.com/view/globalsouthai-neurips26/home 

LatinX in AI 

The LXAI Workshop has been a recognized part of the NeurIPS workshop lineup since 2018. This one-day event is designed to bring together faculty, students, researchers, and professionals for a day of collaboration and knowledge-sharing. The agenda includes invited talks from leading experts, oral and poster presentations of cutting-edge research, a panel discussion on key topics in the field, and a dedicated mentoring session.

Each year, we receive high-quality paper submissions from Latinx researchers worldwide, demonstrating the community’s growing strength and interest in AI. We aim to amplify Latinx voices and promote diverse perspectives to build a more inclusive and equitable AI research ecosystem. While our focus is on Latinx representation, the event is intentionally inclusive and open to all who are committed to advancing diversity in AI.

While all presenters will identify primarily as LatinX, everyone is invited to attend.  

LatinX in AI will be present across Atlanta and Sydney venues: 

Sydney – December 7th

Atlanta –  December 9th

For more details, please visit: https://www.latinxinai.org/neurips-2026 

Muslims in ML 

The 7th Muslims in ML (MusIML) Workshop will be held at NeurIPS 2026 in Sydney, bringing together the community at the intersection of machine learning, Sovereign AI, and global Muslim expertise. Since 2020, MusIML has organized 12 events at top-tier conferences, growing steadily from around 100 attendees at our first workshop to 60 accepted papers and 300+ attendees at NeurIPS 2025.

The workshop is dedicated to promoting ethical and Sovereign AI solutions tailored to diverse cultural, linguistic, and economic contexts, and creating a dedicated academic space for Muslim researchers. This year’s program spans a broad range of contributions from Sovereign ML for Muslim communities and Islamic contexts, to AI system demonstrations, social-impact competition proposals, and open ML research by Muslim scholars, alongside our mentored-research initiatives (Ibtikar × MusIML and the Fatima Fellowship) and a panel on “AI and the Future of Society: Sovereignty and Global Equity.” Beyond the main workshop in Sydney, we will also host social events at NeurIPS 2026’s two satellite sites, Atlanta and Paris, for the global community.

Support for attending NeurIPS 2026 is available through the NeurIPS Affinity Program and MusIML, with priority given to authors of accepted papers presenting in person. 

Muslims in ML will be present across Paris and Sydney venues: 

Sydney – December 7th

Paris –  December 10th 

For more details, visit https://www.musiml.org/events/2026-NeurIPS/index.html

New in ML

In an era deeply influenced by the rapid rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative AI, how can researchers effectively navigate their journey in machine learning and accelerate their growth to achieve impactful breakthroughs? The NewInML Workshop brings together emerging researchers and senior PhD students, connecting them directly with top experts and industry thought leaders for profound insights and practical guidance. Covering topics from foundational skills to advanced research in LLMs and Generative AI, the workshop offers a unique opportunity to enhance your research capabilities and competitive edge. Join us to ride the wave of innovation and grow alongside the brightest minds in the ML community! 

NewInML will be present only at the Paris venue on December 11th. For more details, visit our official website: https://newinml.github.io/NewInML2026NeurIPS/

Queer in AI 

The Queer in AI workshop and social events at NeurIPS 2026 aim to create a vibrant and inclusive space that brings together queer students, researchers, and practitioners from across the globe to critically examine the impact of AI on the LGBTQIA* community. The workshop aspires to build a strong network of queer individuals, enable discussions at the intersection of AI and queer identities, and tackle issues of discrimination within the tech industry and society at large.

The Queer in AI workshop is dedicated to advancing equitable AI practices and contributing to a future where technology serves the needs of all communities. The workshop is committed to advocating for a more ethically grounded approach to AI development, ensuring that diverse voices are heard and valued in conversations about the future of technology. 

Queer in AI will be present across all venues: 

Sydney – December 9th

Atlanta – December 11th

Paris –  December 10th 

For more details, please visit our official website: https://www.queerinai.com/neurips-2026 

Women in ML 

Women in Machine Learning is proud to celebrate nearly two decades of driving gender diversity in AI, since our founding in 2006. WiML’s flagship Annual event is held alongside NeurIPS, providing a space where women can connect, learn, and grow. The field of machine learning, while growing immensely in scale and scope over the last decade, still faces a major lack of gender diversity. WiML’s mission is to close this gap by creating opportunities for women and non-binary scholars to engage in substantive technical and professional conversations, while increasing awareness of their achievements in the community.

The WiML Workshop at NeurIPS 2026 brings this mission to life, celebrating research across the breadth of ML. Our goals are to:

  • Highlight the contributions of women and non-binary scholars across the breadth of ML
  • Create spaces to meet, exchange ideas through deep technical discussion, and spark future collaborations
  • Provide junior researchers with a visible platform to present their work to peers and senior members of the community

The program features invited talks by women and non-binary researchers, a poster session showcasing accepted abstracts and fostering interactive feedback, and dedicated networking time to build lasting connections. Structured mentorship sessions round out the program, offering practical guidance on navigating publishing, shaping research agendas, and exploring academic and industry career paths. Through these sessions, women starting out in their careers can gain valuable guidance, while established women serve as a guiding force, sharing their experience and paying it forward to the next generation.

Our workshop is designed to be welcoming to researchers at all stages and across subfields. WiML will be present across all three venues: Atlanta, Paris, and Sydney. 

Sydney – December 8th

Atlanta – December 9th

Paris –  December 10th

For more details, please visit the WiML website and our 2026 workshop website.

September 16 2026

Join Us at NeurIPS 2026: Financial Assistance and Volunteer Applications Are Now Open

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference

NeurIPS is at its best when people from across our community can participate fully, presenting their work, exchanging ideas, finding collaborators, and helping make the conference possible.

We are excited to announce that applications for NeurIPS 2026 Financial Assistance and conference volunteering are now open.

NeurIPS 2026 will bring our community together across Sydney, Atlanta, and Paris, alongside opportunities for virtual participation. We recognize that the cost of attending an international conference can be a significant barrier. Through Financial Assistance and volunteer opportunities, the Neural Information Processing Systems Foundation aims to make it possible for more members of our community to participate.

What is new for 2026?

The NeurIPS program now includes many different forms of research, scholarship, creativity, service, and community participation. This year, we have updated the Financial Assistance application to better reflect that breadth.

Applicants may report all relevant NeurIPS 2026 contributions they would like the committee to consider, including contributions to the:

  • Main Track
  • Evaluations & Datasets Track
  • Position Paper Track
  • Creative AI Track
  • Reproducibility/MLRC Track
  • Education Track
  • Other official NeurIPS 2026 programs

Each program has its own contribution and presentation formats, and an eligible contribution does not need to be a conventional conference paper.

The application also asks applicants to identify and rank only the conference locations they could realistically attend. This will help us match available support with applicants who can use it, while reducing the need for late changes.

Financial Assistance

Financial Assistance is intended for members of the NeurIPS community for whom participating in the conference would create a meaningful financial burden.

Decisions may consider financial need, career stage, first-time in-person attendance, verified NeurIPS contributions and service, prior assistance used, location-specific travel burden, and the overall applicant pool. We particularly encourage applications from students, junior postdoctoral researchers, first-time attendees, and others who would be unable or unlikely to participate without support.

Available assistance may include:

  • Complimentary in-person conference registration
  • Complimentary virtual registration
  • Prepaid accommodation in Sydney, Atlanta, or Paris

Accommodation is subject to availability and will be arranged directly for selected recipients. Financial Assistance does not cover flights, trains, local transportation, meals, per diem, independently booked accommodation, or other expenses purchased by the applicant.

Before selecting a location, applicants should carefully consider travel authorization requirements, travel time, transportation costs, accessibility or personal constraints, and expenses not covered by an award. In-person awards are location-specific and cannot be transferred from one conference location to another. Recipients should also promptly notify the organizers if they can no longer attend or use any part of their award so that the support can be reallocated. 

Apply for Financial Assistance 

Volunteering

Volunteers play an important role in creating a welcoming, accessible, and well-organized conference experience. Volunteering is also an opportunity to meet other members of the community, gain behind-the-scenes conference experience, and contribute directly to making NeurIPS 2026 a success.

Volunteer applications are available for Sydney and Atlanta. Volunteers are normally assigned two shifts of approximately four hours each at the conference venue, and volunteer support does not include accommodation or travel expenses.

Applications for Paris will open in late September with a separate volunteering campaign. Please follow official NeurIPS Paris communications for details on how to apply for those volunteer opportunities. The application link and additional details will be posted on the main NeurIPS website when available.

For Sydney and Atlanta, volunteers must purchase their NeurIPS registration before the conference and will be refunded after completing their shifts at the conference. 

Applicants may apply for both Financial Assistance and volunteering. The two applications are separate, and any obligations associated with an award or volunteer assignment will be communicated directly to selected applicants.

Apply to Volunteer

Key dates

• Applications open: 7 September 2026

• Application deadline: 6 October 2026, Anywhere on Earth

• Financial Assistance decisions: 14 October 2026, Anywhere on Earth

• Volunteer decisions: 20 October 2026, Anywhere on Earth 

Please read the complete NeurIPS 2026 Financial Assistance and Volunteering FAQ before applying. The FAQ includes additional information about eligibility, available support, contribution reporting, accommodation, registration, location selection, accessibility-related follow-up, and what happens after an award is accepted.

We warmly encourage eligible members of our community to apply and to share this announcement with students, researchers, and contributors who may benefit from these opportunities.

We look forward to welcoming you to NeurIPS 2026, in Sydney, Atlanta, Paris, and online, and to building an engaging and accessible conference together.

NeurIPS 2026 Next Generation & Accessibility Chairs
Apoorva Beedu, Ehsan Adeli, Ismini Lourentzou, Nicolas Papadakis, and Vineeth N. Balasubramanian

September 8 2026

NeurIPS Foundation Announces 2026 Bridging the Future Grants Program Recipients

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference

The Neural Information Processing Systems Foundation is excited to announce the recipients of the NeurIPS 2026 Bridging the Future Grants Program, created to support innovative activities that broaden participation in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). Open to learners at every stage, from grade school students taking their first steps in computational thinking to senior faculty developing new pedagogical approaches, the six recipients of this year’s program were selected from 134 applications submitted from organizations and individuals around the world. 

The winning projects were selected for their global relevance, innovation, and novel approach that has not been widely implemented in AI/ML education and outreach. 

The NeurIPS 2026 Bridging the Future Grants Recipients

  • Aderonke Sakpere

AI and Data Science for Her: Training the Next Generation of High School Girls in Nigeria

This program will train 300 Nigerian high school girls across six geopolitical zones of the country in the fundamentals of AI and data science. Grounded in published research on how teenage girls engage with technical subjects, the curriculum is deliberately girl-centered, pairing students with female mentors already working in AI, and connecting technical concepts to capstone projects addressing real challenges in healthcare, agriculture, and education. AI clubs formed in each participating school will keep the learning going long after the program’s formal end.

  • Aleksei Komissarov 

The Voice-Native Classroom: Multilingual AI Co-Teachers for Global ML Education

Most AI tutoring tools ask students to type, which is a barrier for learners working in a second language. This project builds a voice-native AI co-teacher that converses with students in their own language, and is available at any time of the day. Already piloted in a live university course since September 2025, the approach will now scale to reach more than 1,000 students across 50+ countries through Neapolis University in Cyprus and DataTalks.Club, a Berlin-based online community of 80,000 learners – with no tuition and no language barrier standing between students and rigorous ML education.

  • Sermin Kalafat 

DTCH (Digital Turcology and Cultural Heritage) 

DTCH Digital Turcologist Bootcamp Historical Turkic languages, including Ottoman Turkish, Old Uighur, and Chagatai, are vastly underrepresented in the AI world. Researchers in this field have lacked the shared benchmarks and documented datasets that make AI results comparable and reproducible. This 12-week online bootcamp addresses that directly, training 18–24 researchers, librarians, and heritage professionals to apply AI to historical manuscripts responsibly – building evidence packs, benchmark kits, and reproducible notebooks that anyone can verify. All materials will be published openly so communities working with other under-resourced historical languages can run the same program themselves.

  • Tushar Shinde 

The 100x Challenge: Compression-First Research Pipeline for Bandwidth-Constrained Regions

Rather than treating limited computing infrastructure as an obstacle, this program treats it as a design constraint worth building around. Researchers across Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, and Ethiopia will learn to compress AI models to run on basic smartphones and low-cost hardware, then apply those skills in small research teams tackling problems in medical imaging, agriculture, and efficient ML theory, with mentorship from Stanford, Oxford, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University guiding teams toward publication-ready work.

  • Piera Riccio 

FATE-AI: Futures of Agriculture, Technology, and Ecology in Artificial Intelligence

Set in a rural farming community in the Matese National Park region in Southern Italy, where students have studied in temporary classrooms since a 2013 earthquake, this project pairs a 30-hour AI course grounded in agricultural applications with a one-month artist residency. The result is an interdisciplinary approach that teaches technical skills alongside critical, ethical thinking about technology’s role in farming communities, leaving behind both new capabilities and a lasting piece of public art.

  • Jon Saraydar

Wikair (Student-Led Nonprofit), a Global, Youth-Led, Interdisciplinary AI Education Program

Wikair trains high school students to teach AI workshops to other students – connecting the subject to psychology, art, ethics, media, and business along the way, not just code. With 10-20 free workshops planned across at least five U.S. states and a fully open-access curriculum library released to the public, this peer-educator model shows how far a lean, volunteer-powered budget can reach.

Each of these projects reflects something we hoped to see when we opened this program: a willingness to meet learners where they are, rather than asking them to clear barriers built for someone else’s circumstances. We look forward to following their progress over the coming year and sharing updates as these programs reach their first cohorts of students and researchers.

If you have questions about the NeurIPS Bridging the Future Grants Program, or are interested in future funding cycles, please reach out to the NeurIPS Foundation at: bridging-the-future@neurips.cc.

We are grateful to everyone who took the time to share their vision with us, and look forward to continuing to invest in creative, impactful initiatives that broaden participation in AI and machine learning.

NeurIPS Foundation

NeurIPS Newsletter – August 2026

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference

Welcome to the August edition of the NeurIPS monthly Newsletter!

The NeurIPS Newsletter aims to provide an easy way to keep up to date with NeurIPS events and planning progress, respond to requests for feedback and participation, and find information about new initiatives. This newsletter will focus on NeurIPS 2026, held in Sydney, Australia, with official Satellites in Atlanta, USA and Paris, France. The conference will be held on the following dates:

  • Sydney, Australia: from Sunday, Dec 6th to Saturday, Dec 12th
  • Atlanta, USA: from Tuesday, Dec 8th to Sunday Dec 13th
  • Paris, France: from Wednesday, Dec 9th to Sunday Dec 13th

You are receiving this newsletter as per your subscription preferences in your NeurIPS profile. As you prepare to attend NeurIPS, we hope that you will find the following information valuable.

  1. Calling AI Science Communicators: NeurIPS 2026 Education Track

    We’re inviting science communicators in AI to submit proposals to teach an emerging technical concept. Concepts can be any technical idea that has underpinned a large set of papers at top-tier AI conferences over the past year, from new architectures to training and alignment techniques to evaluation and reasoning methods. Think the 2026 equivalents of the Transformer, the reparameterization trick, or LLM judges. You don’t need to be the original author of the concept, just able to explain it with real clarity.

    Accepted proposals must be paired with original teaching materials (code notebooks, demos or short videos) and will be presented as part of a full-day primer in Sydney on 7 December 2026, ahead of the main NeurIPS conference. All materials will be gathered in an open repository, free for the community after the conference.

    Submissions close 4 September 2026 AoE (Anywhere on Earth).

August 27 2026

Navigating NeurIPS 2026: A Breakdown of the Multi-Site Registration Process

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference

With NeurIPS 2026 adopting a distributed, multi-site format across Sydney, Atlanta, and Paris, managing attendance is a significant logistical challenge. Given the size of the conference, our primary goal is to provide fair access to participants worldwide while allocating registrations across the three venues.

To help clarify the process, here is a breakdown of how registration allocations will work this year for authors, committee members, and the general public.

Let’s start with the question likely to be on everyone’s mind. When will registration open for the general public?

Registration for the Sydney and Atlanta sites will open on Thursday, September 3rd, at 23:00 AEST. The Paris registration system is currently undergoing separate testing by our Paris and EventHost teams, and we will announce its opening date soon. 

Please take note of the time zone and try to register as early as possible to secure your spot. We selected this time with the aim of making registration reasonably accessible to as many members of our global community as possible. The following describes the process for registrations for each participant type. 

1. Guaranteed Spots for Presenting Authors in the Core Tracks

For the core tracks (Main, Evaluations & Datasets, Position Papers, Journal-to-Conference, and Reproducibility), we guarantee exactly one registration spot per accepted paper. This spot is reserved for the designated author to present the work. Other co-authors need to register on their own as part of the general public (see below).

Prior to the acceptance announcements, the program chairs and our EventHost team will distribute a form to all authors to collect their preferred presenting locations. Within this form, the authors will nominate one of the authors as the designated author to present, together with their preference of location and other details. This data will help us move quickly once decisions are made to assign locations. We realize that it is unusual to start collecting information early, but we also appreciate your support in helping speed up the process for authors of accepted papers to start making travel arrangements.

Please be assured that your location preferences will have absolutely no impact on the chance of your paper being accepted. As we note below, although we will do our best to accommodate the site preferences of authors of accepted papers, we cannot guarantee that everyone will get their top choice.

Shortly after paper decisions are announced, our team will set a deadline for each paper presenter to update the form if needed. Poster locations will then be assigned to best accommodate these preferences. If a site reaches capacity, the available slots will be allocated with a randomized process that takes necessity and preference into account; therefore, top-choice locations cannot be guaranteed. The designated presenting author will receive guaranteed registration tied exclusively to their allocated poster site. Please note that due to the massive scale and operational complexity of NeurIPS, no changes to the presenting author or poster location will be permitted once allocations are finalized.

If the designated author has registered already for a different location than the one designated for their paper, they will have to cancel their registration (and receive a full refund until the  deadline of Nov. 4) and register to the designated location (they will have a guaranteed spot). Note that we expect the designated author to be present at the designated location to present their work. 

2. Reserved Allocations for Additional Contributions

NeurIPS thrives on the specialized communities built around its other tracks. Each accepted contribution in one of the Workshops, Competitions, Creative AI, or Education tracks receives one reserved registration allocation for its authors. As with the main tracks, this reservation is tied to the specific site where the contribution is scheduled to be presented.

To make this work, workshop organizers (as well as  competition organizers, Creative AI chairs, and Education chairs) must import their accepted contributions into the NeurIPS website by the  deadlines established by our EventHost team. The guaranteed registration applies only after those contributions have been successfully linked to the  authors’ NeurIPS site accounts. Registration cannot be guaranteed if the relevant organizers or chairs miss the deadline. We will provide further details separately to the organizers, chairs, and authors. 

3. Committee Members and Complimentary Passes

Running a multi-site conference of this magnitude requires a massive volunteer effort. To recognize this, NeurIPS will offer complimentary registrations to our organizing team and top-performing members of the program committee (reviewers, Area Chairs, and Senior Area Chairs for the Main, ED, and PP tracks). The registrations are guaranteed and will be processed shortly after the paper-acceptance decisions are announced. If the recipients of these registrations had already previously registered, an automatic refund will be issued. 

To provide track support, workshops, competitions, and other tracks (Social/Affinity/Creative AI/Education/Reproducibility) will receive a fixed number of complimentary registrations. These are strategically allocated to ensure the track’s program will be running smoothly and accounted for at their respective sites.

4. General Public Registration

For members of the broader community that do not fall in any of the categories above, registration will be offered on a first-come-first-served basis. Through this blog post, we hope to announce the opening of registration sufficiently in advance to allow  everyone to plan ahead. In addition, we will create a waitlist for those who are unable to secure a place. Given that individuals can wear many hats (for instance, authors, part of the organization committee), and that plans can change, we do expect a reasonable number of additional registration to become available after the registration deadline. We will exclusively rely on the waiting list to fill these additional spots. The waiting lists will be specific to the different locations, and one person can only be on one of the three different waiting lists. Once we have more clarity on the number of additional registration spots available we will contact those selected from the waiting list, offering them the opportunity to register. To promote fairness, we will randomize the order, while still giving some weight to the original position in the waiting list. We therefore strongly recommend that you try to register as soon as possible to maximize your likelihood of attending the conference. 

We hope that this experimental process for this year’s first-ever three-site NeurIPS’s conference will promote fairness and increase accessibility. We look forward to hearing feedback from the community to improve the process in future years.

August 11 2026

Meet the Organizing Team Behind NeurIPS 2026

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference

Every year, the Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) relies on the incredible dedication, vision, and hard work of our volunteer organizing committee. We are so excited to introduce the wonderful group of researchers, practitioners, and leaders who will bring NeurIPS 2026 to life!

Earlier this year, we put out a Call for Organizer Nominations, and we were truly moved by the community’s response. We received hundreds of applications from passionate people eager to share their time and expertise. To everyone who applied: thank you so much for your willingness to step up and serve.

We’d like to share a bit with the community about the process of building the organizing team. The Program Chair team was built by our Senior Program Chair, Finale Doshi-Velez, following her appointment by and interactive discussions with the NeurIPS Board. The rest of the team was built by the General Chairs through a thoughtful and collaborative process. It began by gathering nominations from our open call, along with recommendations from trusted members of our community. We then carefully reviewed every single application and recommendation to understand each candidate.

As a first step, given NeurIPS growth, we started by identifying a senior, experienced member for each team. The senior member typically has served in a similar role at past NeurIPS conferences or other major venues and is able to pass down institutional knowledge which is key to making the conference a success. Once these senior members were in place, we engaged in detailed discussions with them to identify the best candidates to form their respective teams. The NeurIPS Board reviewed and advised on all these choices to ensure balance, diversity, and excellence before formal invitations were sent to each candidate.

Additionally, since NeurIPS 2026 is experimenting with satellite events in Atlanta and Paris, alongside the main conference in Sydney, we also invited our Satellite Chairs and Satellite Program Chairs to nominate team members wherever needed. Working together in this way allows for transparent decision-making across all locations, ensuring that every track at our satellite events is executed with the same high standards of scientific excellence as the main Sydney site.

Last but not least, some teams have chosen to invite junior members of the community to serve as Assistant Chairs. They conduct hands-on work to assist the chairs of each team and experience the impact of serving the community at an early stage in their careers. We thank them for their efforts and look forward to their continuous growth with NeurIPS.

We are incredibly grateful to the diverse group of individuals who have agreed to take on these vital roles. To see the full roster of individuals who are making NeurIPS 2026 happen, please visit the official NeurIPS 2026 Committees Page. On behalf of our biggest organizing committee ever, we look forward to welcoming you to NeurIPS 2026 across our global locations in Sydney, Atlanta, and Paris!

NeurIPS 2026 General Chairs
Hsuan-Tien Lin and Razvan Pascanu

August 10 2026

Announcing the NeurIPS 2026 Workshops

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference

We are excited to announce the list of NeurIPS 2026 workshops. We received 477 submissions (454 valid), a significant increase over last year’s numbers. From this great batch of submissions, we have accepted 102 workshops: 48, 28, and 26, to be hosted in Sydney, Paris, and Atlanta, respectively. The acceptance rates were 21.5%, 25.4%, and 23.6% for Sydney, Paris, and Atlanta, respectively. These variations reflect different numbers of submissions for each location and different numbers of rooms available per venue. 

The workshops will take place on:

  • Fri Dec 11 and Sat Dec 12, 2026 – Sydney
  • Sat Dec 12 and Sun Dec 13, 2026 – Paris and Atlanta

Given the exceptional quality of submissions this year, we wish we could have accepted many more workshops. We want to thank everyone who put in tremendous effort in submitting a workshop proposal. We would also like to thank the reviewers who worked tirelessly to assess all proposals.

Selection Process

In making our selections, we asked the reviewers to closely follow our Guidance for Workshop Proposals, which was also shared with the proposal authors via the call for proposals. Workshop proposals must be reviewed somewhat differently from academic papers, and hence we asked the reviewers to consider both scientific merits and broader impacts in their assessments, including fitness for NeurIPS, potential for high impact, originality and novelty, quality and clarity, organizers’ quality, speakers’ quality, diversity and quality of logistics. We invited 1021 high-quality reviewers (mostly from past years’ top-reviewer lists) and managed to recruit 353. Each proposal had at least 2 assigned reviewers, whose reviews were summarized into metareview feedback.

Individual reviewers’ evaluations of proposals were important in the decision process, but they were not the only considerations. We also strove for a good balance among research areas, applications, and theory. As interest across research areas varies, some areas were more competitive than others.

This year, we also collected organizers’ preferences for workshop venues. With the exception of a handful of workshops that received their secondary preferred location, we were able to satisfy the primary preference constraints. 

This year we introduced two constraints to safeguard the quality of workshops: we disallowed more than 8 organizers per workshop, and prohibited any organizer from being listed on more than 2 proposals. The vast majority of organizers followed these rules with the exception of 5 cases.

The next step is your contributions! Several workshops have begun soliciting submissions, many using our suggested submission date of Aug 29, 2026. We typically let each workshop advertise its own call for papers (if they plan to include workshop papers). We will communicate some additional deadlines to the workshop organizers to facilitate the successful planning of 102 exciting workshops. Stay tuned for more technical and contextual information coming soon!

NeurIPS Newsletter – July 2026

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference, NeurIPS Newsletters neurips2026, newsletter

Welcome to the July edition of the NeurIPS monthly Newsletter!

The NeurIPS Newsletter aims to provide an easy way to keep up to date with NeurIPS events and planning progress, respond to requests for feedback and participation, and find information about new initiatives. This newsletter will focus on NeurIPS 2026, held in Sydney, Australia, with official Satellites in Atlanta, USA and Paris, France. The conference will be held on the following dates:

  • Sydney, Australia: from Sunday, Dec 6th to Saturday, Dec 12th
  • Atlanta, USA: from Tuesday Dec 8th to Sunday Dec 13th
  • Paris, France: from Wednesday Dec 9th to Sunday Dec 13th

You are receiving this newsletter as per your subscription preferences in your NeurIPS profile. As you prepare to attend NeurIPS, we hope that you will find the following information valuable.

This NeurIPS Newsletter includes:

  1. Competition Track Decisions Announced
  2. Call for Social Events
  3. Clarification on the Rebuttals and Author Discussion
  4. Creative AI track deadline Extension
  5. Upcoming Workshop Decisions

  1. NeurIPS 2026 Competition Track Decisions Announced
    • The NeurIPS 2026 competition track decisions were announced: the program includes competitions ranging from Scientific AI, Physics, and Engineering, to Healthcare, Biology, and Humanitarian Applications, to Foundation Models, Reasoning and AI Evaluation, to Robotics, Agents and Embodied AI.
    • For the details and more information on the decisions, read our blog post: https://blog.neurips.cc/2026/07/28/neurips-2026-competitions-announced/ 
    • For any questions, concerns, or feedback, please contact competition-chairs@neurips.cc
  2. NeurIPS 2026 Call for Social Events
    • NeurIPS is soliciting proposals for social events at NeurIPS 2026. NeurIPS social events are community-led events that help attendees connect, exchange ideas, build collaborations, and create lasting memories beyond the technical program. Whether you’re a first-time organizer or a seasoned community builder, we encourage you to submit your idea by September 5, 2026. Let’s make NeurIPS 2026 an unforgettable experience—together! Learn more and submit your proposal: NeurIPS 2026 Call for Socials.
    • For any questions, concerns, or feedback, please contact  social-chairs@neurips.cc
  3. Clarification on the Rebuttals and Author Discussion
    • A clarification on the timeframe for rebuttals and author discussion, for all three tracks at NeurIPS 2026.

      Rebuttals can be posted until August 3rd AOE. This includes any back and forth with the reviewers. The “rebuttal” button and “official comment” button will both be treated equivalently – the difference in terminology between the two is to facilitate discussion during the discussion period on OpenReview. This also means you are allowed to post several comments, with a total of over 10000 characters.

      Please post your answers to the Area Chair’s initial-meta reviews via a comment from July 28th and by August 3rd, so that reviewers can see it too.

      We emphasize that the entire period from July 27 through August 3 AOE is time for authors to respond to reviews, including with additional results or other responses to reviewers as applicable. It is your choice how you wish to divide this time into initial rebuttals and subsequent discussion with reviewers and ACs.
  4. Creative AI track deadline Extension
    • To accommodate submissions that may require additional preparation time, the NeurIPS 2026 Creative AI Track is extending its submission deadline by one week, to August 10, 2026, Anywhere on Earth (AoE).

      For more information, please refer to https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForCreativeAI
  5. Upcoming Workshop Decisions
    • The decisions for the workshops will be posted in early August followed by a blog post – stay tuned!

July 28 2026

NeurIPS 2026 Competitions Announced

Communication Chairs 2026 2026 Conference

We are delighted to announce the competitions that have been accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 Competition Track. As in previous years, the selection process was highly competitive, with many outstanding submissions spanning a broad range of machine learning research areas and real-world applications. After a careful review process, we selected 16 exceptional competitions that reflect both emerging directions in AI research and long-standing challenges across science, engineering, and society, as listed below.

This year marks the tenth edition of the dedicated NeurIPS Competition Track. Whether you are participating in a NeurIPS competition for the first time or are a returning competitor, this year’s competition list offers exciting opportunities for researchers, practitioners, and students from a wide variety of backgrounds and expertise. We encourage everyone to explore the competitions and consider participating.

Competitions play a unique role in advancing machine learning research by bringing together communities around well-defined, impactful challenges for fair comparison of methods. They foster collaboration, encourage reproducible research, and provide shared benchmarks that accelerate progress across diverse domains.

As a participant, you will have the opportunity to engage with an active research community, develop new technical skills, and work on problems with meaningful real-world impact. Many past competitions have led to widely used benchmark datasets and open-source resources, scientific progress through the validation of impactful research directions and lasting collaborations. We hope this year’s competitions will continue that tradition.

Following the pattern from previous years, organizers of accepted competitions will have the opportunity to publish post-competition analyses either through the NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks Track or through a dedicated PMLR volume for NeurIPS competitions, providing a venue to document insights, benchmark results, and lessons learned from the challenges.

The NeurIPS 2026 program includes the following exciting competitions:

Scientific AI, Physics, and Engineering

  • Learn2Design 2026: A Physics Experiment Design Competition for Gravitational Wave Detectors
  • The Smart Buildings Challenge: Learning Foundation Models for Real-World Optimization at Scale
  • Fusion Equilibrium Challenge: Inferring & Transferring Magnetic Geometry without Magnetic Diagnostics
  • NeurIPS 2026 RealPDE Competition: Scientific ML for Real-World Physical Systems
  • FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge on Distribution Shifts in Cosmology

Healthcare, Biology, and Humanitarian Applications

  • Synthetic Humanitarian Surveys at Scale (SimulacraBench): A Closed Evaluation via Unreleased UN Microdata
  • AMP Challenge: A Benchmark for Generative AI in Antimicrobial Peptide Design
  • Speech Accessibility Project Challenge 2
  • The Virtual Embryo Challenge: Generative Modeling of Embryogenesis Across Space, Scale and Time

Foundation Models, Reasoning, and AI Evaluation

  • The Steerability Challenge
  • Predictive AI Evaluation Competition
  • AIMO Interpretability Challenge
  • QuantiPhy Challenge: Quantitative Physical Reasoning for VLMs

Robotics, Agents, and Embodied AI

  • RoboSynChallenge: Mastering Real-World Dexterity via Generalizing Synthesized Manipulation Skills
  • RoCo-Spring: The Robust Correspondence Challenge
  • Agenthon 2026: Verifiable AI for Quantitative Finance

We are deeply grateful to all of the reviewers and members of the Competition Track Program Committee who dedicated their time and expertise to evaluating this year’s proposals. We congratulate the organizers of the accepted competitions and sincerely thank everyone who submitted a proposal for contributing such high-quality ideas.

If you have any questions or suggestions regarding the Competition Track, please feel free to contact competition-chairs@neurips.cc. 

We look forward to the outcomes of this year’s competitions and to welcoming organizers and participants at NeurIPS 2026. 

NeurIPS 2026 Competition Track Chairs
Jes Frellsen, Shou-de Lin, Annika Reinke

Welcome to the June edition of the NeurIPS monthly Newsletter!

The NeurIPS Newsletter aims to provide an easy way to keep up to date with NeurIPS events and planning progress, respond to requests for feedback and participation, and find information about new initiatives. This newsletter will focus on NeurIPS 2026, held in Sydney, Australia, with official Satellites in Atlanta, USA and Paris, France. The conference will be held on the following dates:

  • Sydney, Australia: from Sunday, Dec 6th to Saturday, Dec 12th
  • Atlanta, USA: from Tuesday Dec 8th to Sunday Dec 13th
  • Paris, France: from Wednesday Dec 9th to Sunday Dec 13th

You are receiving this newsletter as per your subscription preferences in your NeurIPS profile. As you prepare to attend NeurIPS, we hope that you will find the following information valuable.

This NeurIPS Newsletter includes:

  1. Updates in the Position Paper Track
  2. Reminder of Call for Ethics Reviewers
  3. Call for Tutorials
  4. Call for Affinity Events

  1. Updates in the Position Paper Track
    • The Call for Paper of NeurIPS 2026 Position Paper Track requires papers to be substantially human-written, with AI used only for copy-editing or similar peripheral changes to the main text. The Position Paper Track chairs took a conservative approach, noting that excessive AI use in writing submitted position papers may create risks for peer review, including added verification burden for reviewers and questions about attribution.
    • To assess whether authors were largely abiding by this policy, the Position Paper Track chairs partnered with Pangram, under an enterprise-level data agreement ensuring that zero data would be retained. After several independent analyses to verify the model and rule out scenarios with significant false positives, the chairs made the difficult decision to uphold the policy: 178 submissions, or 18.4%, will be desk rejected, while 123 submissions, or 12.7%, will be asked to provide evidence of substantial human engagement or risk desk rejection.
    • The blog post lays out the analyses informing this decision and shares the organizers’ perspective.
  2. Reminder of Call for Ethics Reviewers
    • NeurIPS is recruiting Ethics Reviewers for NeurIPS 2026!
    • If you have experience critically evaluating potential risks and harms in machine learning research, and can provide thoughtful feedback on broader impacts, please read our Call for Reviewers and consider volunteering as an ethics reviewer. You can also directly volunteer here: NeurIPS 2026 Ethics Reviewer Self-Nomination – Fill out form
    • Please share with qualified and interested colleagues! The scale of the conference continues to grow, so we are always seeking to grow our pool of ethics reviewers.
  3. Call for Tutorials
    • NeurIPS is calling proposals for in-person tutorials, please send your proposals before July 3rd, 2026, AOE. Read more about this year’s guidelines here: https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/CallForTutorials
    • Whether you are planning to send a proposal or not, let us know what topics you would like to see covered in tutorials by filling our survey: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScG3y-x_I_7nd7FOD9kAsiqnhMW8vsLUe9MivTOzgwXoU-E_Q/viewform?usp=header
  4. Call for Affinity Events
    • NeurIPS is calling proposals for affinity events at NeurIPS 2026. Affinity groups interested in organizing an event are invited to submit the Application Form and signed Agreement Form by June 28th, 2026, AOE, to affinity-chairs@neurips.cc.
    • For any questions, concerns, or feedback, please contact affinity-chairs@neurips.cc.
